importance_ranking.reason: Heavy structural fabrications span visually distinct sub-types — trusses, crane girders, pipe racks, industrial frames — that buyers must identify before reading any text. Fabrication quality, weld finish, and surface treatment are also partially visible in photos, providing a secondary quality signal for project-critical procurement.

Fabrication type, material grade, and inspection standard are primary shortlisting gates — a buyer needing IS:2062 E350 bridge girders with ASME weld inspection cannot substitute a general platform fabricator. Without matching specs, no further evaluation occurs.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall in heavy structural fabrications; buyers search by fabrication capability, certification, and track record rather than manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: ISO 9001 certification, NDT/weld inspection capability, past project credentials, and service location (Pan India vs regional) are evaluated during vendor shortlisting — particularly for government/PSU and EPC buyers who require vendor qualification. Company identity is a trust and eligibility signal, not a brand preference.

Per-kg indicative rates vary substantially with material grade, fabrication complexity, and surface treatment — buyers use listed rates as budget entry points and comparison signals before negotiating project-specific quotes. Indian EPC buyers are price-aggressive but price is only comparable after spec and capability are confirmed.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Large turnkey packages may be quoted per MT (equivalent at scale); discrete machine base frames or equipment skids may be quoted per piece or per set — unit must be shown to prevent price comparison errors across these conventions.
importance_ranking.reason: Per-kg vs per-MT vs per-piece quoting conventions coexist in this category; a buyer comparing rates without knowing the unit cannot make a valid price comparison. Unit is a necessary qualifier for any price shown on the listing.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the primary structural product class (bridge girder vs truss vs plant structure vs platform) — non-interchangeable across project requirements and the single largest driver of price, certification requirements, and fabricator capability.

Material class (Mild Steel vs Stainless Steel vs Alloy Steel) drives a 3–10x per-kg price difference and determines project compliance eligibility — a buyer cannot substitute one material class for another.

missing_important_specs.why_important: IS:2062 E250 / E350 / E410 grades have different yield strengths and project eligibility requirements — buyers specify grade in their drawings and fabricators must confirm material sourcing capability and price accordingly; the existing 'Material' spec captures material type (MS, SS) but not the grade within structural steel.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Routes the RFQ to fabricators with the right structural capability and certification — a bridge girder application requires certified weld inspection and higher-grade steel, while an industrial shed application does not, making this the primary seller-routing signal.

Non-interchangeable structural steel grades (E250 vs E350 vs E410 vs ASTM A36) determine fabricator material sourcing capability and project compliance — sellers need this to confirm they can supply the specified grade and price accurately.

missing_important_specs.why_important: A seller without erection capability cannot respond to a Supply & Erection or Turnkey RFQ — this spec fundamentally routes the buyer to fabricators who can deliver the complete scope, not just supply steel.
Galvanising requires a separate facility not available at all fabricators — sellers need to know if surface treatment is in scope to confirm capability and include it in their quote.

Project scale (tonnage) determines whether a fabricator has the workshop capacity and financial capability to execute — small fabricators cannot handle large-tonnage orders, and large fabricators may decline small jobs.
